dedupe_keys.name: mabdt engine multi agent based digital twin engine for manufacturing operations

description: An open-source runtime for building and running agent-based digital twins of manufacturing operations without commercial simulation software. The Zenodo record says it has four parts: a simulation environment that runs agent populations as hierarchical statecharts, an event-driven communication kernel that links internal messages to IoT devices over MQTT, an interface layer that exposes system state as read-only records, and an application layer for dashboards, IoT commands and queries assisted by large language models. The release holds the deployment-agnostic engine (mabdt), a reference deployment on the Tiger Motors educational assembly line, a minimal toy deployment, a scaling experiment harness and tests, and accompanies the author's PhD dissertation and a paper submitted to the Journal of Intelligent Manufacturing. Version 1.0.0 was published on 19 June 2026 by Michail Katsigiannis as a downloadable ZIP of about 0.3 MB under the MIT licence. Coverage is any factory the user models. Caveats: new research software with one educational reference line, and the implementation language is not stated on the record read. For simulation it gives a free way to couple a factory model with live sensor feeds, to test how outages of power, networks or machines ripple through production. A related catalogue record is AnyLogic.
